item.text: {"claims":[{"id":"c1","text":"In the primary BM25 paper, Robertson and Walker present BM25 as an approximation to the 2-Poisson probabilistic retrieval model that incorporates within-document term frequency, document length, and within-query term frequency into probabilistic weighting, and they report considerable performance improvements over simple inverse collection-frequency weighting on TREC.","required_concepts":["2-poisson","probabilistic_weighting","term_frequency","document_length","query_term_frequency","trec_improvement"],"acceptable_patterns":["2-Poisson","within-document term frequency","document length","within-query term frequency","considerable performance improvements","inverse collection[- ]frequency weighting"],"sources":[{"url":"https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-1-4471-2099-5_24","equivalent_urls":["https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.5555/188490.188561"]}],"evidence_passages":[{"url":"https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-1-4471-2099-5_24","text":"In the primary BM25 paper, Robertson and Walker say their goal is to use the 2-Poisson model to incorporate three variables into probabilistic retrieval weighting: within-document term frequency, document length, and within-query term frequency. They also report that the resulting simple weighting functions produced “considerable performance improvements” over simple inverse collection-frequency weighting on TREC."}],"weight":1},{"id":"c2","text":"An author-written technical note describes BM25 as combining three kinds of per-term evidence into a request-document matching score: collection frequency weight, within-document term frequency, and document length; document scores are the sum of the query-term weights present in the document and documents are ranked by descending score.","required_concepts":["collection_frequency","document_tf","document_length","matching_score","sum_over_query_terms","rank_descending"],"acceptable_patterns":["collection frequency weight","within-document term frequency","document length","matching score","sum of the query-term weights","ranked by descending score"],"sources":[{"url":"https://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/techreports/UCAM-CL-TR-356.pdf","equivalent_urls":[]}],"evidence_passages":[{"url":"https://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/techreports/UCAM-CL-TR-356.pdf","text":"Robertson and Sparck Jones describe BM25 as a formula for combining three kinds of per-term evidence into a request-document matching score: collection frequency weight, within-document term frequency, and document length; `TF(i,j)` as the number of occurrences of term `t(i)` in document `d(j)`; and normalized document length `NDL(j) = DL(j) / Average DL`."}],"weight":1},{"id":"c4","text":"An author-written TREC-4 BM25 variant uses Robertson-Sparck Jones relevance weight w(1), document term frequency tf, query term frequency qtf, and document-length normalization through K = k1((1-b)+b*dl/avdl).","required_concepts":["rsj_weight","tf","qtf","length_normalization","k1","b"],"acceptable_patterns":["w\\(1\\)","qtf","tf","K\\s*=\\s*k1\\s*\\(\\(1-b\\)\\+b\\*dl/avdl\\)","document-length normalization"],"sources":[{"url":"https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2016/02/okapi_trec4.pdf","equivalent_urls":[]}],"evidence_passages":[{"url":"https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2016/02/okapi_trec4.pdf","text":"The author-written TREC-4 paper gives a BM25 variant with these scoring factors: Robertson-Sparck Jones relevance weight `w(1)`, document term frequency `tf`, query term frequency `qtf`, and document-length normalization through `K = k1((1-b)+b*dl/avdl)`. It defines `tf`, `qtf`, `dl`, and `avdl` directly."}],"weight":1},{"id":"c5","text":"The authors explicitly interpret k1 as controlling the influence of within-document term frequency: higher k1 increases TF influence, and k1 = 0 removes TF influence.","required_concepts":["k1","tf_influence","higher_increases","zero_removes"],"acceptable_patterns":["k1","controlling the influence","TF influence","k1\\s*=\\s*0","removes TF influence"],"sources":[{"url":"https://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/techreports/UCAM-CL-TR-356.pdf","equivalent_urls":[]}],"evidence_passages":[{"url":"https://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/techreports/UCAM-CL-TR-356.pdf","text":"The authors explicitly interpret `k1` as controlling the influence of within-document term frequency: higher `k1` increases TF influence, and `k1=0` removes TF influence."}],"weight":1},{"id":"c6","text":"The authors explicitly interpret b as the document-length normalization parameter on a 0 to 1 scale: b = 1 corresponds to treating extra length as repetition or verbosity, while b = 0 corresponds to treating extra length as multi-topic scope; they also report that b = .75 was helpful in TREC.","required_concepts":["b","length_normalization","verbosity","scope","range_0_1","b_.75"],"acceptable_patterns":["b","0 to 1","b\\s*=\\s*1","b\\s*=\\s*0","repetition|verbosity","multi-topic|scope","b\\s*=\\s*\\.75"],"sources":[{"url":"https://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/techreports/UCAM-CL-TR-356.pdf","equivalent_urls":[]}],"evidence_passages":[{"url":"https://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/techreports/UCAM-CL-TR-356.pdf","text":"The authors explicitly interpret `b` as controlling document-length normalization, with `b` ranging from 0 to 1. They say `b=1` corresponds to the assumption that long documents are long because they are repetitive, while `b=0` corresponds to the assumption that long documents are long because they are multi-topic. They further say that moving `b` toward 1 reduces TF’s effect on the view that extra length is mostly verbosity, and they report that `b=.75` was helpful in TREC."}],"weight":1}],"rejected_claims":[{"text":"BM25's original authors gave a clear semantic interpretation for k2.","reason":"Unsupported by the supplied evidence. The codex final answer says clear author-supported interpretations were found for k1, b, and practical use of k3, but not a comparably clear author explanation of k2."},{"text":"Within-query term frequency is always part of core BM25 in every primary formulation.","reason":"Overly broad. The supplied evidence says qtf appears in some author-written Okapi BM25 formulations, while a simplified BM25 form in the Cambridge technical note does not include it."},{"text":"The original papers establish k1 = 1.2 as the default BM25 setting.","reason":"Unsupported by the supplied evidence.
